findings.message: DELIVER_BY is measured on the script clock (SECONDS), but activeDeadlineSeconds counts from Job start. Pod scheduling and the image pull before the agent init container starts are not deducted from the 300 s left after delivery. That 300 s must still cover save_bundle (no timeout), the record calls, and the whole writeback main container, which only starts after the agent init container exits. So the claim that 'the pod still records the failure and saves the bundle before Kubernetes stops it' does not hold. Fix: base the deadline on Job or pod start (stamp it in the manifest or use the downward API), or reserve an explicit margin for pod startup and writeback, and subtract the time already spent before the script began.
findings.scenario: An uncached node takes 280 s to pull the image. The agent runs to FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT (cause=deadline). The remote hangs on every push, so retries run until script time TIMEOUT+300, which is Job time TIMEOUT+580. save_bundle, record and writeback then have 20 s, and the Job is killed by activeDeadlineSeconds. There is no exit=push-failed record, no bundle, and writeback never runs.

findings.message: bundle_held returns 'held' whenever `git bundle list-heads` fails. This treats 'could not read the file' the same as 'not a bundle'. drop_bundle then rm's the pair after a good push, and save_bundle overwrites it. A read failure (permissions, I/O) on a real bundle therefore deletes unpushed commits instead of keeping them. Fix: tell 'not a bundle' (file readable, bad signature) apart from a read error, and keep the file on a read error.

When git push exits non-zero (not 124) with only blank stderr, push-error is written empty. The record then carries `push_error=` with no cause. Write a fallback line such as `push failed: exit <rc>` when the filtered error is empty.

The README presents FLEET_PUSH_TIMEOUT (and implicitly the pause schedule) as a pod env an operator can tune. render_run_env never passes FLEET_PUSH_TIMEOUT or FLEET_PUSH_PAUSES into the Job, and there is no fleet: key for either, so production runs always use 120 s and '5 15 45'. Either say these are fixed or wire them through dispatch.
